topic: Complete common-basal SI-PAG orientation under selection and unknown-target soft interventions. On Dai et al.'s finite causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection twin-graph class, with oracle observational and regime MAGs, construct a fixed D,K-independent sound within/cross-regime endpoint-rule calculus whose monotone closure equals the canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG. Prove every residual circle has opposing realizations from two compatible models sharing one basal selected DAG, and derive polynomially many oracle-input endpoint updates plus simultaneous finite-alphabet CI/invariance-test confidence SI-PAGs under positivity and a separation margin. A global basal-DAG enumerator may certify lemmas but cannot be the headline calculus. Consumer: Dai et al.'s sciPlex2/A549 perturbation analysis, where completeness determines whether remaining circles are biological ambiguity or missing orientations. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Conditional on a feasible ancestral selected set A, preserving basal edges outside E[A] and replacing E[A] by either no edge or one acyclic signature-monotone path preserves all regime skeletons and unshielded colliders. This yields exact selected-selected endpoint witnesses: an arrowhead exactly under intervention membership, and a tail when unaffected or reachable in the signature-monotone selected graph. Exhaustive checks covered 2,664 erasures, 21,312 two-regime families, 102,912 arrow witnesses, 68,160 tail witnesses, 2,997 independent twin projections, and seeded D=4 families without failure; a D=3,K=4 example forces a bidirected triangle only after cross-regime coupling. No checked source proves the common-basal completeness theorem, and v1's global enumerator remains excluded. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Lift the fixed-A construction across unknown selected sets and common exterior DAG completions using a fixed local rule list, preserving every regime fill edge and collider signature without a global realizability query. EARLY KILL TEST: Compare the explicit rule list with exact endpoint invariance on all normalized D<=3,K<=2 families, the D=3,K=4 bidirected-triangle witness, and bounded D=4,K=3 cases with varying A; for each residual circle construct both witnesses without guessing A or querying global feasibility. open_problems.open_problem: Is there a fixed, dimension- and regime-count-independent set of within-regime and cross-regime endpoint rules whose monotone closure equals the canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG for common-basal pre-treatment selection with unknown-target soft interventions?

source_refs.claim: CDIS is sound, but the paper explicitly leaves completeness and an equivalence-class graphical representation unresolved.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Shows that I-FCI is incomplete even with known soft-intervention targets; complete recovery uses compatible-MAG enumeration, while new local rules only tighten the result.
source_refs.author: Zihan Zhou, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: Provides a finite sound-and-complete orientation calculus for a single observational PAG with latent confounding and selection bias.
source_refs.author: Jiji Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dai et al.'s regime MAGs must jointly lift to one basal selected DAG with unknown intervention targets. Applying Zhang's complete PAG rules regime by regime loses this common-basal coupling, while Zhou and Kocaoglu assume known targets and still require enumeration for full completeness. The literature scan found no finite local calculus that simultaneously handles pre-treatment selection, unknown targets, and synchronized common-basal realizability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite rule list with soundness and closure-completeness proofs for every invariant endpoint, together with a theorem that every endpoint left circular by closure is non-invariant over the common-basal model class.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination model, the selection-before-intervention motivation, and the sciPlex2/A549 application whose unresolved circles need a completeness interpretation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Subjects are selected before perturbation -> ordinary augmented graphs misstate the resulting CI and invariance patterns -> twin graphs and CDIS restore soundness -> a complete local SI-PAG calculus is needed to separate genuine biological ambiguity from missing orientations.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive endpoint rules from discriminating and uncovered-path configurations, then prove completeness by constructing MAG representatives for remaining circle marks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem is the common-basal, multi-regime analogue of complete observational PAG endpoint orientation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use intervention-node semantics to derive cross-environment orientation rules and compare their closure against a complete enumeration oracle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates how soft-intervention semantics compel endpoints beyond ordinary FCI, though with known targets and no pre-treatment selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Uniformly control CI tests and propagate their correctness through an FCI/RFCI graph search under sparsity and separation assumptions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once an oracle SI-PAG calculus is fixed, its empirical version similarly needs graph-level correctness from a family of CI and invariance decisions.

open_problems.open_problem: Does every circle endpoint remaining after sound SI-PAG closure admit opposing realizations in two intervention families that share one basal selected DAG, rather than merely in independently compatible regime MAGs?

source_refs.claim: Defines equivalence through intervention-specific twin graphs constructed from a basal DAG and intervention targets, while leaving CDIS completeness unproved.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Characterizes Markov equivalence of individual MAGs through adjacencies and ordered colliders and gives a polynomial equivalence test.
source_refs.author: R. Ayesha Ali, Thomas S. Richardson, Peter Spirtes

source_refs.claim: Constructs valid local transformations for listing representatives of one observational MAG equivalence class.
source_refs.author: Tian-Zuo Wang, Wen-Bo Du, Zhi-Hua Zhou

open_problems.why_unsolved: Single-MAG equivalence and local mark-change results do not preserve the stronger fiber constraint that every regime projection must arise from one basal DAG and selected set. Flipping a circle in one regime can change intervention descendants, selection-induced fill edges, or collider signatures elsewhere. The scan found no synchronized common-basal mark transformation or opposing-witness theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a constructive theorem mapping every residual circle to two common-basal compatible models with opposite endpoint marks and identical oracle inputs, or a finite counterexample proving that residual-circle semantics require a richer graphical representation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its twin-graph formulation makes clear that compatibility is joint across regimes and rooted in one pre-intervention causal system.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A PAG circle ordinarily records variation across compatible MAGs -> intervention-specific MAGs here are not freely combinable -> every realization must share a basal selected DAG -> residual circles require common-basal opposing witnesses.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize MAG equivalence through adjacencies, unshielded colliders, and collider paths with order, then use those invariants to certify a proposed mark change.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired witness construction must preserve these MAG invariants simultaneously in every regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Use minimal potentially directed and discriminating paths to construct representatives witnessing that unoriented PAG endpoints genuinely vary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Common-basal opposing witnesses are the synchronized multi-regime analogue of the representative step in observational PAG completeness.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate uniform accuracy of CI decisions into consistency of all reported PAG marks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An empirical opposing-witness interpretation requires confidence that a retained circle is due to model ambiguity rather than a testing error.

open_problems.open_problem: Can all invariant SI-PAG endpoints be computed with polynomially many oracle-input endpoint updates without enumerating the potentially exponential family of common-basal DAG or regime-MAG completions?

source_refs.claim: Its theoretically complete known-target soft-intervention procedure has worst-case cost depending on the number of MAGs compatible with the learned partial graph.
source_refs.author: Zihan Zhou, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: Lists all MAGs with polynomial delay using singleton background knowledge, but the represented equivalence class may contain exponentially many MAGs.
source_refs.author: Tian-Zuo Wang, Wen-Bo Du, Zhi-Hua Zhou

source_refs.claim: Determines equivalence of two supplied MAGs in polynomial time, which does not compute all invariant endpoints of a jointly constrained multi-regime class.
source_refs.author: R. Ayesha Ali, Thomas S. Richardson, Peter Spirtes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Polynomial equivalence testing and polynomial-delay enumeration are weaker than producing the invariant endpoint summary in total polynomial time. Common-basal compatibility also couples orientation choices across regimes, so single-regime MAG listing cannot be invoked independently. The scan found enumeration-based completeness for known targets and output-sensitive MAG listing, but no polynomial endpoint-closure algorithm for unknown-target pre-selection twin graphs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An algorithm returning the canonical SI-PAG with a polynomial bound in the number of observed vertices, regimes, and oracle CI/invariance inputs, plus a proof that its updates orient exactly the endpoints shared by all common-basal compatible models.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the precise tradeoff between complete enumeration and inexpensive but incomplete local orientation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sound local rules leave compelled endpoints circular -> enumeration restores completeness but inherits equivalence-class size -> large intervention problems cannot pay exponential output cost -> compute only the invariant SI-PAG through polynomially many updates.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode an endpoint choice as singleton background knowledge, apply locally complete propagation rules, and recursively list valid completions with polynomial delay.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The donor identifies local validity checks that avoid brute-force invalid orientations; the destination must quotient away enumeration and synchronize the checks across regimes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use compact ordered-collider invariants to test MAG equivalence in polynomial time.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A polynomial SI-PAG algorithm needs similarly compact certificates for whether an endpoint is forced across the jointly constrained class.

method_exemplars.technique: Restrict expensive FCI searches while proving asymptotic correctness of every reported causal mark.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a template for separating computational savings from correctness of the endpoint information ultimately reported.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a simultaneous finite-sample confidence SI-PAG for finite-alphabet data under positivity and a uniform CI/invariance separation margin, with coverage for every endpoint produced by adaptive orientation closure?

source_refs.claim: CDIS is justified at the oracle and faithful-distribution level and evaluated empirically, without simultaneous finite-sample endpoint coverage.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Obtains confidence guarantees for causal-parent conclusions by intersecting models whose predictions are not rejected as invariant across environments.
source_refs.author: Jonas Peters, Peter Bühlmann, Nicolai Meinshausen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Develops nonasymptotic discrete conditional-independence tests, reproves optimality without Poissonization, and supplies Monte Carlo calibration.
source_refs.author: Ilmun Kim, Matey Neykov, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: Test-level guarantees do not automatically survive adaptive graph search: one mistaken separating set or invariance decision can generate many false arrowheads through closure. Invariant causal prediction controls a different causal-parent object, while discrete CI testing treats individual hypotheses rather than the joint within- and cross-regime query family induced by an SI-PAG algorithm. The scan found no endpoint-wise simultaneous confidence object for selection-coupled intervention PAGs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A data-dependent partially oriented graph with a theorem that, with probability at least 1-alpha, every displayed tail and arrowhead belongs to the oracle canonical SI-PAG, together with an explicit sample-size bound in alphabet size, positivity, margin, dimension, and number of regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates turning invariance tests into a confidence-valued causal object instead of reporting an unqualified point estimate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal mechanisms should remain stable across environments -> finite samples make invariance decisions uncertain -> invert a test family to retain confidence-supported causal conclusions -> construct an endpoint-wise confidence SI-PAG.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nonasymptotically controlled discrete CI statistics without Poissonization and calibrate them through Monte Carlo permutations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Under finite alphabets and a separation margin, each within-regime oracle CI can be replaced by an explicitly controlled finite-sample decision.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert environment-invariance tests and intersect accepted models so that the aggregate causal conclusion inherits coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The SI-PAG confidence object must likewise aggregate many invariance decisions without losing simultaneous validity.

method_exemplars.technique: Control a graph search's family of CI errors under sparsity and strong-separation assumptions, then prove consistency of the resulting PAG.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest graph-level template for propagating uniform test accuracy through an FCI-style orientation algorithm.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the endpoint-invariant equivalence class, and is there a complete local learner for it, when unknown-target soft interventions occur after common pre-treatment selection but the basal causal graph also contains latent common causes?

source_refs.claim: Handles pre-treatment selection and unknown-target soft interventions but assumes causal sufficiency among the measured variables.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Gives a graphical characterization and sound-and-complete learner for unknown-target soft interventions in non-Markovian systems, without pre-treatment-selection twin-world semantics.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Murat Kocaoglu, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Introduces FI-Markov equivalence, F-PAGs, and sound-and-complete F-FCI for latent confounding with post-treatment selection, a different temporal regime from basal twin graphs.
source_refs.author: Gongxu Luo, Loka Li, Guangyi Chen, Haoyue Dai, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest theories cover complementary boundaries: Jaber et al. allow latent confounding and unknown soft targets but do not encode selection fixed in a counterfactual basal world, whereas Dai et al. encode that timing but assume causal sufficiency. Marginalizing latent causes inside a twin graph can create inducing paths whose endpoints and collider order change under intervention-descendant splitting, so applying psi-FCI separately to selected regime distributions need not preserve a common basal latent DAG. Luo et al.'s complete F-PAG concerns post-treatment selection and does not close this timing gap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph representation and equivalence criterion for latent common-basal selected twin models, followed by either a finite sound-and-complete orientation calculus or a counterexample proving that no PAG-like endpoint summary represents the class.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the destination selection timing and explains why ordinary intervention graphs fail when enrollment precedes perturbation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pre-treatment selection changes intervention-induced dependence patterns -> twin graphs encode the counterfactual selected population -> causal sufficiency excludes latent biological regulators -> characterize the latent-confounded common-basal equivalence class.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode unknown targets with intervention nodes, characterize psi-Markov equivalence using MAG structure, and prove maximal orientation of the learned equivalence class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the latent-confounded unknown-target margin; the first changed proof step is ancestral projection after basal-world splitting and selection conditioning.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine PAG semantics with intervention-sensitive edge types and prove soundness and completeness using selection/intervention response symmetries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates that latent confounding plus selection timing can require a richer equivalence-class diagram, albeit for post-treatment selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish high-dimensional consistency for PAG recovery with latent and selection variables through uniform control of CI decisions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A learner for latent selected twin graphs would need an analogous empirical-consistency rung after its oracle equivalence theory is established.

literature_map:
Dai et al. (ICLR 2025, arXiv:2503.07302) introduce pre-treatment-selection interventional twin graphs and sound CDIS for unknown-target soft interventions, but explicitly leave completeness and equivalence-class representation open.
Zhang (Artificial Intelligence 2008, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2008.08.001) proves arrowhead and tail completeness of a finite orientation-rule system for a single observational PAG under latent confounding and selection.
Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes (Annals of Statistics 2009, arXiv:0908.3605) characterize MAG equivalence by adjacencies and ordered colliders and give a polynomial equivalence test.
Richardson and Spirtes (Annals of Statistics 2002) establish ancestral-graph projection semantics for latent and selection variables, the single-regime substrate used by PAG theory.
Kocaoglu et al. (NeurIPS 2019) characterize known-target soft-intervention equivalence with latent variables and give sound orientation rules.
Jaber et al. (NeurIPS 2020) extend the framework to unknown targets through psi-Markov equivalence and prove sound-and-complete recovery without pre-treatment twin-world selection.
Squires, Wang, and Uhler (UAI 2020, arXiv:1910.09007) characterize unknown-target interventional MECs and give consistent UT-IGSP under causal sufficiency, motivated by genomic off-target effects.
Yang, Katcoff, and Uhler (ICML 2018, arXiv:1802.06310) characterize general known-target intervention MECs for DAGs but do not address selection or common-basal MAG coupling.
Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (JMLR 2020, arXiv:1611.10351) provide the JCI multi-context framework for imperfect and unknown-target interventions, without the sharper completeness guarantee needed here.
Zhou and Kocaoglu (ICML 2026, OpenReview dVfJSLGTYm) show known-target I-FCI is incomplete; complete recovery uses MAG enumeration, while added local rules only tighten the result.
Wang, Du, and Zhou (ICML 2024; ICML 2025) develop valid local MAG transformations and polynomial-delay MAG listing, but listing remains output-sensitive and does not enforce one basal DAG across regimes.
Colombo et al. (Annals of Statistics 2012, arXiv:1104.5617) prove sparse high-dimensional consistency for FCI/RFCI, providing graph-level asymptotic inference but not simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs.
Peters, Bühlmann, and Meinshausen (JRSSB 2016, arXiv:1501.01332) invert invariance tests into confidence-valid causal-parent conclusions; Kim et al. (EJS 2023, arXiv:2308.05373) give practical nonasymptotic discrete CI tests.
Luo et al. (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2509.25800) give complete F-PAG/F-FCI theory for latent confounding with post-treatment selection, leaving pre-treatment common-basal selection distinct.
Srivatsan et al. (Science 2020, doi:10.1126/science.aax6234) provide sciPlex2/A549 perturbation data, where endpoint completeness affects whether circles represent biological ambiguity or algorithmic incompleteness.
